fields.columns: | columns event.time, event.type, site.name, agent.uuid, src.process.storyline.id, src.process.user, src.process.uid, src.process.cmdline, src.ip.address, src.port.number, dst.ip.address, dst.port.number, src.process.parent.cmdline, tgt.process.cmdline
fields.description: This rule detects execution of PowerShell scripts located in the "C:\Users\Public" folder
fields.name: Execution of Powershell Script in Public Folder
fields.notes:
- To move around freely without attracting too much attention, attackers often use reliable software (one of the favorites is psexec) that looks normal in an enterprise environment.
- Use the following aggregate to easily group by endpoint: `| group array_agg_distinct(dst.ip.address) by endpoint.name, src.process.cmdline`
fields.query: event.type="Process Creation" and (endpoint.os="windows" and ((tgt.process.image.path contains "\powershell.exe" or tgt.process.image.path contains "\pwsh.exe") and (tgt.process.cmdline contains "-f C:\Users\Public" or tgt.process.cmdline contains "-f \"C:\Users\Public" or tgt.process.cmdline contains "-f %Public%" or tgt.process.cmdline contains "-fi C:\Users\Public" or tgt.process.cmdline contains "-fi \"C:\Users\Public" or tgt.process.cmdline contains "-fi %Public%" or tgt.process.cmdline contains "-fil C:\Users\Public" or tgt.process.cmdline contains "-fil \"C:\Users\Public" or tgt.process.cmdline contains "-fil %Public%" or tgt.process.cmdline contains "-file C:\Users\Public" or tgt.process.cmdline contains "-file \"C:\Users\Public" or tgt.process.cmdline contains "-file %Public%"))) | columns tgt.process.cmdline
